scope_note: SG-MA-PHARMACIST-ADMINISTRATION after a further correction following the V10ZB audit. The section now gives, once, the definition of serious adverse drug event that M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c) adopts from M.G.L. c. 111, s. 51H(a) (an untoward, preventable occurrence associated with a drug that results in one of the listed outcomes, with the statute's "may be considered" for an occurrence that later develops into one), notes that 247 CMR 2.00 has no separate definition, and sets it apart from the circular's own list of events to report to the prescriber at once. Every later use of the term, including the safe course, now reads it by s. 51H: orientation[8], comparison_tables[5], retrieval_prompts[25]-[26], decision_logic[13], exceptions[8], common_traps[22], role_duties[9], quick_review[18] and learning_objectives[7]. comparison_tables[2].rows[6] and [3].rows[0] now attribute the circular's conditions to every listed medication and 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9)(a)-(d) only to mental health and substance use disorder treatment drugs, and quick_review[8] drops a qualifier the circular does not use. New rule: MA-SERIOUS-ADVERSE-DRUG-EVENT-DEFINITION. Scope gate: every actionable signal declined; they are collaborative drug therapy management prescribing, MA-PHARMACIST-PRESCRIBER-ID, contraception and expedited partner therapy records, and other 247 CMR 2.00 definitions (MA-DRUG-SAMPLES-NOT-FOR-RESALE, MA-PERSON-PRACTITIONER-DEFINITIONS, MA-PHARMACIST-NABP-EPROFILE) taught in other sections. All six practice links stay.
